Willem de Kooning marries Elaine Fried
De Kooning marries the art student Elaine Fried.
Marriage of Elaine Fried and Willem de Kooning
After a devoted courtship and Sunday dinners in Sheepshead Bay, despite Elaine's mother's reservations about Bill's worth, they marry in 1943.
Marriage of Elaine and Willem de Kooning

A minimal wedding on the morning of December 9, 1943. Elaine, 25, wears a navy blue dress she already owns and borrows her sister's handbag; the ring costs $9.50. Her mother does not attend (Elaine is “too young”); her brother Conrad stays away out of indifference, the couple already living together. Witnesses: Charles Fried, Peter Fried, Janice Biala and Daniel Brustlein, Max Margulis, Bart Vanderschellen. Elaine remembers that the group then went to a bar; other sources say that Biala and Brustlein, newly married themselves, gave a wedding lunch in a downtown cafeteria.
Pharmacology studies, then dropping out

Enters the university on his parents' advice to study pharmacology; drops out because of the difficulty of the courses (he does not yet know he is dyslexic) and his refusal to dissect a live frog in biology class.

Marriage to Elaine and settling on 22nd Street

They marry in December 1943 and settle in a top-floor loft on 22nd Street, long left empty, which de Kooning repairs and fixes up himself over six months — the only long pause in his painting. A wedding present for Elaine. Late rent and the sale of the building later force them to move to an apartment on Carmine Street (Greenwich Village) and a studio for Willem on Fourth Avenue, behind Grace Church.
